methodology: Milestones are included only when a repository, release, paper, merged pull request, registry decision, or other public record supports the wording. Repository creation proves that a repository entered the GitHub record; it does not by itself prove a product launch. Organization-reported chronology is identified as approximate when the surviving record does not establish an exact date. Date precision is stated for every entry.

entries.title: The earliest surviving Elixpo project record
entries.description: The OctaBit repository is the earliest surviving public project record now held by Elixpo. It documents the college-era hardware work that predates the GitHub organization and supports the statement that Elixpo has been building in public since 2023.

entries.title: The Elixpo GitHub organization is created
entries.description: A shared organization gives the growing project series a durable public home. This is the beginning of the organization record, distinct from the earlier college projects that were later gathered under it.

entries.title: The Chapter repository begins preserving shared work
entries.description: The elixpo_chapter repository becomes the master collection for project history and cross-project contributions. It later supplies the evidence base used for contributor recognition across the organization.

entries.title: Elixpo participates in its first recorded Hacktoberfest
entries.description: Elixpo maintainers open the Chapter to Hacktoberfest work, apply the programme labels, review submissions, and record accepted changes. Three Hacktoberfest-labelled pull requests are merged during the month; the record supports maintainer-led participation, not an official role within the Hacktoberfest programme itself.

entries.title: The Pollinations relationship becomes part of Elixpo's infrastructure story
entries.description: Elixpo records 2024 as the beginning of its relationship with Pollinations.AI and currently identifies Pollinations as an infrastructure partner. The surviving public record verifies the partnership and later shared infrastructure, but does not establish an exact 2024 start day, so this date remains organization-reported and approximate.

entries.title: A versioned Chapter release is published
entries.description: Elixpo Chrome Extension 5.0 is published from the Chapter repository. It remains an early example of the organization recording a concrete public release instead of treating repository activity as the outcome by itself.

entries.title: Research becomes a public Elixpo workstream through OctaBit
entries.description: The RISC-style eight-bit breadboard computer is documented in a journal paper alongside its public implementation, schematics, component notes, and EEPROM tooling. It establishes the first surviving published research record in the Elixpo timeline; the portal records the paper's stated venue without implying an independently verified peer-review process.

entries.title: A second Hacktoberfest opens a much larger contribution cycle
entries.description: The Chapter merges 47 Hacktoberfest-labelled pull requests from 24 GitHub accounts during October. Maintainers administer the repository programme by preparing work, reviewing submissions, applying acceptance labels, and merging eligible changes; the resulting record marks Elixpo's shift to sustained outside contribution at scale.

entries.title: Public services and shared infrastructure enter the organization record
entries.description: Repositories for LixBlogs, LixSketch, member portfolios, Accounts, Lixrl, Oreo, Payouts, mail, administration, and service status are added to the organization. Their creation dates verify when they entered this record, not necessarily when every underlying project first began.

entries.title: Community support becomes a documented in-kind programme
entries.description: Elixpo formalizes event partnerships for stickers, artwork, social credit, and short project introductions, and publishes the terms openly. This programme is non-monetary: Elixpo does not currently solicit, accept, hold, or route organization-level sponsorship funds, and support cannot purchase selection, research outcomes, contributor credit, or governance authority.

entries.title: OreoLook publishes its caching architecture
entries.description: The OreoLook research record connects an arXiv preprint on three-layer caching, the operated answer engine, an interactive Hugging Face Space, and a released evaluation dataset while keeping the limits of reproducibility explicit.

entries.title: Reproducible research becomes a first-class public surface
entries.description: QFabric and MonoDiffuse publish technical records with code, artifacts, methods, limitations, citation information, and documented reproduction paths. They establish the standard expected from research presented through Elixpo.

entries.title: Elixpo adopts the project-foundry direction
entries.description: The organization defines its enduring purpose around active open work, public Chapters, independent Member Projects, reproducible research, operated services, releases, and attributable contribution records rather than becoming a conventional SaaS portfolio.

entries.title: Lifecycle states and the Open Field identity are made explicit
entries.description: A canonical registry distinguishes active, paused, maintenance, archived, and cancelled work instead of hiding closures. On the same date, Open Field is approved as the shared visual system while product identities and the historical branding repository remain independently traceable.

entries.title: Elixpoo v2 defines the automation boundary
entries.description: Elixpo publishes its organization-wide GitHub project-management agent as a bounded automation system for allowlisted triage, exact-mention assistance, comment-only pull-request review, Discussion support, and merged-change memory. The contract explicitly excludes product-code implementation and keeps sensitive decisions under human authority.

entries.title: Crumb becomes Elixpo's autonomous agent harness
entries.description: Elixpo fixes Crumb's direction as a self-hosted Rust agent harness and natural language terminal powered by Pollinations. Crumb owns its execution loop, permissions, memory, tools, sessions, checkpoints, and supervision locally, while keeping native shell commands independent from model or network availability.
